access_continuity_justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an administrator of this repository and a reviewer of its publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The user interfaces are entropy.collect_rolls, a dice prompt in the terminal built on input() and print(), and the command python -m bip39_slip39, which reads rolls with getpass. Their prompts are plain text with no colour or layout, so any screen reader the terminal supports reads them as written. The command clears the screen around a SLIP-0039 share and does not echo rolls. There is no GUI and no web front end. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md#limitations-not-vulnerabilities
assurance_case_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md gives the threat model (what is defended, the adversaries, what is not defended), the trust boundaries, the secure design principles and the common implementation weaknesses with what counters each, naming the file, test or workflow behind every argument. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: test.yml runs the test suite on every pull request that changes more than prose and on every push to main that changes more than top-level Markdown files, and its aggregate job `test: every job passed` is a required check. It runs on one interpreter; the os-ubuntu, os-macos and os-windows workflows run the supported interpreters weekly and at a release. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
build_non_recursive_justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_preserve_debug_justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_repeatable_justification: Every week sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its tag. It passes only if the rebuilt file matches the release's attested digest byte for byte. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_reproducible_justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit and normalized by .github/scripts/normalize_sdist.py. sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its tag every week and verifies it against the release's build-provenance attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/actions/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: This tree builds no native binaries -- it is pure Python on the uv_build backend -- so there is no compiler or linker invocation for CC/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
bus_factor_justification: fametrano wrote almost all of the code and is the only person who knows it in depth. The claude account in the contributors graph comes from the Co-Authored-By trailer on AI-assisted commits, almost all of them fametrano's. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, did the 2026-09-30 security review, approves pull requests and has made one small commit to this repository. In the last year, outside contributors have made only small changes. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, has made no commit to this repository. The organization owners administer every repository. Knowledge of the code rests on fametrano alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/graphs/contributors
code_of_conduct_justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/REVIEWING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run as pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs the same .pre-commit-config.yaml in CI as a required check, so the style is enforced automatically rather than by review alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
coding_standards_justification: pyproject.toml selects every ruff rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and runs mypy in strict mode. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the public-surface, input-validation, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: fametrano is the only significant contributor. In the last year, outside contributors have made only small changes. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, has made one small commit to this repository. pmazzocchi and fametrano are associated: both are CheckSig co-founders, as their GitHub profiles state. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, has made no commit to this repository. https://github.com/fametrano https://github.com/pmazzocchi
copyright_per_file_justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", and ruff's flake8-copyright rule (CPY001) keeps it there, e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/src/bip39_slip39/__init__.py
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The algorithms are fixed by the specifications the package implements -- a BIP39, SLIP-0039 or Electrum sentence has to stretch to the seed every other implementation computes -- so there is no alternative algorithm a user could switch to without leaving the standard. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/README.md
crypto_call_justification: Every primitive is called from the standard library -- hashlib's sha256, sha512 and pbkdf2_hmac, hmac, secrets and os.urandom -- and none is reimplemented. What the package writes itself is only what the specifications define above those primitives: SLIP-0039's GF(256) interpolation and its Feistel structure, and the mnemonic encodings. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/tree/main/src/bip39_slip39
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: bip39-slip39 performs no network communications -- nothing under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib -- and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/tree/main/src/bip39_slip39
crypto_credential_agility_justification: bip39-slip39 is a library with no configuration file or credential store: entropy, mnemonics, passphrases and shares are caller-supplied function parameters, never read from or written to a file this project owns. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
crypto_floss_justification: no closed source dependencies: the standard library alone
crypto_keylength_justification: Every default meets 112 bits: bip39.mnemonic_from_entropy draws 128 bits when given none, electrum's generator draws 132 bits rounded up to whole words, and slip39 refuses a master secret under 128 bits. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/tree/main/src/bip39_slip39
crypto_password_storage_justification: does not store passwords: a passphrase is stretched into a seed and handed back, never stored or used to authenticate anyone
crypto_pfs_justification: implements no network key-agreement protocol: the package performs no network communications at all
crypto_published_justification: Every mechanism is a published one: BIP39 (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, SHA-256 checksum), SLIP-0039 (Shamir sharing over GF(256), an HMAC-SHA256 digest share, a four-round Feistel network whose round function is PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256) and Electrum's seed schemes (HMAC-SHA512 version prefix, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, and the pre-2.0 iterated SHA-256), each checked against the vectors its authors publish. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/README.md
crypto_random_justification: Every random draw comes from the operating system's CSPRNG: secrets for BIP39's and Electrum's default entropy and the simulated dice, and os.urandom for SLIP-0039's default entropy_source. Nothing under src/ uses the random module. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
crypto_tls12_justification: bip39-slip39 performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/tree/main/src/bip39_slip39
crypto_used_network_justification: bip39-slip39 does not use the network: nothing under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/tree/main/src/bip39_slip39
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: bip39-slip39 performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/tree/main/src/bip39_slip39
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or MD5 appears under src/: the hashes are SHA-256 and SHA-512, alone, in HMAC or in PBKDF2, with the iteration counts the specifications fix (BIP39's and Electrum's 2048, SLIP-0039's 10000 * 2^e, the pre-2.0 Electrum scheme's 100000). https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/tree/main/src/bip39_slip39
dco_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s commits are exempt. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
delivery_mitm_justification: Distribution channels use HTTPS exclusively: GitHub, and PyPI through Trusted Publishing. [osps_br_03_02]
delivery_unsigned_justification: Releases are published to PyPI and GitHub Releases and installed with pip from PyPI, all over HTTPS. No package or hash is fetched over plain HTTP. https://pypi.org/project/bip39-slip39/ https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/releases
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot version updates cover uv, github-actions and docker, and Dependabot security updates are on. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
description_good_justification: bip39-slip39 implements the mnemonic schemes of bitcoin wallets, BIP39, SLIP-0039 and Electrum's, from the entropy to the seed, in typed Python. https://btclib.org/bip39-slip39/
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
documentation_achievements_justification: README.md links the OpenSSF Scorecard, Best Practices and Baseline badges on the lines the organization standard reserves for them. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md gives the layers bottom-up: exceptions and _utils, entropy and mnemonic, the schemes bip39, electrum and slip39, none importing another, and dispatch. README.md says the package imports nothing but the standard library, and its What is here maps each scheme to its module. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/README.md#what-is-here
documentation_basics_justification: README.md says what the package holds and what it does not, how to install it, and gives a first use that tests/readme_test.py runs; CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md and ASSURANCE_CASE.md cover the rest. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/README.md
documentation_current_justification: The docs build is gated in CI as a required check (docs.yml, `-n -W`), tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module has no API page, and tests/readme_test.py runs every Python block of README.md, so neither the reference generated from the docstrings nor the README's example can drift from the code. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml
documentation_interface_justification: Every public module and function carries a docstring, gated by ruff's pydocstyle rules and pydoclint, and docs/source's automodule pages render them into the API reference published at https://bip39-slip39.readthedocs.io/; tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from them.
documentation_quick_start_justification: README.md's *A seed from a mnemonic, and a secret split into shares* is a first use -- a BIP39 sentence from entropy, its seed, its scheme recognized, and a SLIP-0039 2-of-3 split recombined -- and tests/readme_test.py runs it, so it is the one the suite checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/README.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, is reviewed every September and states what is maintained, what is intended and what is deliberately not. This repository's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md's Limitations, not vulnerabilities states the known limits: secret material is not zeroized, nothing is constant-time, randomness comes from the operating system, and the dice collector is interactive. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: pytest, the mutation runs and the ClusterFuzzLite targets run Python without -O, so every assert is checked. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No fuzzing or mutation-testing finding is open, and the weekly fuzz and mutation runs on main pass. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/actions/workflows/mutation.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Every release runs the test suite before it is published. release.yml calls test.yml, and the PyPI upload runs only if it passes. The suite fails below 100% coverage, branches included. ClusterFuzzLite fuzzing and cosmic-ray mutation testing also run every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
enhancement_responses_justification: Contributions are answered and merged: https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/pull/28, an outside contributor's fix, was merged the day it was opened.
external_dependencies_justification: pyproject.toml declares `dependencies = []` -- the package imports the standard library alone, which tests/imports_test.py asserts of every module -- and the test and tooling dependencies in its dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, documents the decision model and every role a contributor, reviewer or owner holds; this tree's README.md links it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: https://btclib.org/bip39-slip39/ is served over HTTPS with Content-Security-Policy (frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security. The repository on github.com sends all four. PyPI's project page https://pypi.org/project/bip39-slip39/ sends all but the CSP; that is PyPI's to set. The documentation site https://bip39-slip39.readthedocs.io/ is served by Read the Docs over HTTPS with Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and no Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options; that is Read the Docs' to set. Measured with curl -sIL on 2026-11-01.
hardening_justification: ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules, so a hardening defect such as unsafe deserialization or shell injection fails the lint gate. CodeQL also runs on every pull request and every push to main. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
implement_secure_design_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* applies Saltzer and Schroeder's principles one by one -- economy of mechanism, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, open design, least privilege, psychological acceptability -- each to the file or test that carries it. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
input_validation_justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid with a Bip39Slip39TypeError or Bip39Slip39ValueError, as CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* requires; tests/input_validation_test.py drives the rule over every public function, and tests/fuzz_test.py holds every decoder to it on hostile sentences. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_common_justification: `python -m pip install --upgrade bip39-slip39` installs it from PyPI, as README.md says, and pypi-install.yml installs the published version on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows after each release and weekly. https://pypi.org/project/bip39-slip39/
installation_development_quick_justifica: `uv sync` installs the whole development environment in one command, uv being the only tool to install first; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* section gives it beside `uv run pytest` and the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is `pip install`, which follows pip's and the interpreter's own install-location conventions; there is no project-specific installer that could diverge from that convention. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
interfaces_current_justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated constructs, and pytest turns every warning into an error. deps-latest and deps-oldest run the suite weekly at the newest and the floor versions. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
internationalization_justification: The mnemonic sentence comes in every language the specifications give a word list for: BIP39's reference lists, with Japanese joined by the ideographic space BIP39 requires, and Electrum's own. The language is read back off the words. SLIP-0039 defines English alone. entropy.collect_rolls takes a lang parameter and shows its prompts in all 12 BIP39 languages, translated and checked with AI, as issue #94 decided. The messages of python -m bip39_slip39 and the refusals are in English. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/issues/94 https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/src/bip39_slip39/_rolls_prompts.py
know_common_errors_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md lists the common implementation weaknesses, such as CWE-209 and CWE-330, and what counters each: https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer wrote ASSURANCE_CASE.md, which applies Saltzer and Schroeder's principles to the code one by one. It was reviewed by another owner in https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/issues/26.
license_location_justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/LICENSE>.
license_per_file_justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/src/bip39_slip39/__init__.py
maintained_justification: Pull requests merge every week, and fixes ship in tagged releases. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/releases
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported (SECURITY.md). RELEASING.md runs griffe check against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists what a user must act on to upgrade. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: detect-secrets baseline gated by pre-commit, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection enabled on the repository: https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and accepts only secure methods, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
osps_ac_02_01_justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand, through an issue in btclib-org/.github that an owner other than the one asking approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor, fametrano, holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the approval but still refuses a direct push, so nobody pushes to main directly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. The mention job holds a secret on any pull request's issue comment, and there checks out the default branch. It answers only users with write access, and its tools exclude Bash, edits, writes and file reads. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: Two workflows take workflow_dispatch inputs. mutation.yml's profile is a choice from a fixed list. verified-signatures.yml's before and after reach the run: step only through env:, and the step refuses a value that is not a hexadecimal commit sha. A release tag's name is checked against the package version before anything is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-verified-signatures.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release has a unique calendar version (YYYY.M.D), set by a signed v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that disagrees with the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/releases
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name: the sdist, the wheel, the CycloneDX SBOM and the attestation bundle. The attestation binds each asset to its digest. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/releases/latest
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://bip39-slip39.readthedocs.io/.
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/bip39-slip39/
osps_br_04_01_justification: The GitHub release body is RELEASE_NOTES.md's entry: what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included. CHANGELOG.md lists every change. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Python dependencies come from PyPI, and the required test check runs the suite with uv from the committed uv.lock with --locked. pre-commit installs its hooks at the revisions .pre-commit-config.yaml names. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. The GitHub release carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle over each asset's SHA-256. The tag is signed. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/releases/latest
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_br_07_02_justification: A secret is an environment secret that only the owners reach. A secret kept in any other store is recorded in the REPOSITORY.md of the repository that uses it, and btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded one. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected. The secrets kept outside an environment are rotated before they are a year old, and the list is reviewed yearly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_do_01_01_justification: The user documentation is README.md's *A seed from a mnemonic, and a secret split into shares*, whose Python blocks tests/readme_test.py runs, and the API reference on Read the Docs. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/README.md#a-seed-from-a-mnemonic-and-a-secret-split-into-shares https://bip39-slip39.readthedocs.io/
osps_do_02_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report form asks for what a report needs. SECURITY.md sends a vulnerability to a private channel instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml
osps_do_03_01_justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release assets, and RELEASING.md the check that rebuilds the sdist from its tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_03_02_justification: The verify command pins the signer: --owner names the organization, the output's sourceRepositoryIdentifier must equal this repository's id, --signer-workflow names the organization's reusable-build.yml (reusable-attest.yml for earlier releases) and --source-ref the release tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, a fix ships as a new release, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_05_01_justification: SECURITY.md: only the latest release is supported, so a release stops receiving security updates when the next one is published. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_06_01_justification: The package has no runtime dependency: pyproject.toml declares dependencies = []. uv obtains the development dependencies from PyPI and pins them in uv.lock, and Dependabot tracks them weekly with a seven-day cooldown. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci
osps_do_07_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_01_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md's Roles names who holds access to sensitive resources. fametrano is the maintainer. Every owner, named there by login, is an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_01_02_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, describes the maintainer, owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Proposed changes and usage obstacles are discussed publicly in the repository's GitHub issues (with a question form) and pull requests; cross-repository questions go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% line and branch coverage, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: A grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_le_01_01_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer, Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s aside. Web commits are signed off automatically. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/bip39-slip39/
osps_le_03_01_justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: The LICENSE file ships inside every release asset: the sdist root and the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature; linear history and no force-pushes on main keep that record from being rewritten. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies, none at run time and the development tools in dependency groups, and the committed uv.lock pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_02_02_justification: The release is pure Python. Every GitHub release attaches a CycloneDX SBOM, generated from the built wheel and covered by the release attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/releases/latest
osps_qa_03_01_justification: main requires the listed status checks. enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without them is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The organization standard's section 2 (*Which repositories, and how far*) lists every repository of btclib-org and its tier, and the organization profile lists the published packages. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far
osps_qa_04_02_justification: The project has no additional subproject repository: each release is built from this one repository, and the package has no dependencies.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable is committed. The only binary file is the Sphinx inventory python.inv.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: No executable, library or compiled file is committed. The only binary file is docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, which is not code.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: test.yml's aggregate check ('test: every job passed') is a required status check on main, and it runs the test suite on every pull request except one that changes only the prose files test.yml's prose-pattern names, which no job reads. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite. *Reproducing what CI runs* gives each job's command, and *What gates a merge, and what only reports* says which workflows run on a pull request, on a push and on a schedule, and which of them gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_06_03_justification: The policy is 100% line and branch coverage (CONTRIBUTING.md, standard section 8). pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, so untested new code fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author before a merge to main, and dismisses an approval on a new push. Its bypass list holds one actor, fametrano, in pull_request mode, at rest: the organization-wide bypass the maintainer kept on 2026-11-04 (btclib-org/.github#2021 and btclib-org/.github#2040), read with gh api repos/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/rulesets on 2026-11-07. GOVERNANCE.md reserves that bypass for an emergency, and it is used for ordinary work: over the last two releases, 25 of the 59 pull requests merged had no approval from anybody other than their author (v2026.11.2 14 of 26, v2026.10.24 11 of 33). https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_sa_01_01_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md gives the package's modules, their layers bottom-up and what each may import. ASSURANCE_CASE.md's Threat model and Trust boundaries name the actors, the caller and the adversary, and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#trust-boundaries
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The API reference at https://bip39-slip39.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module, and tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from it. CONTRIBUTING.md's The public surface states what is public.
osps_sa_03_01_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: what is claimed, the threat model, the trust boundaries and how each common implementation weakness is countered; SECURITY.md's limitations section records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names the assets, adversaries and what is not defended, and *Trust boundaries* maps the attack surface where untrusted input enters, each argument naming the file, test or workflow behind it. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels, a GitHub security advisory or email, and the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. A report triaged as easy to rediscover is fixed as soon as possible, and its advisory is published with the fix. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org. GOVERNANCE.md's Roles says that address reaches every organization owner. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository, each naming the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/security/advisories
osps_vm_04_02_justification: The CycloneDX SBOM a release attaches lists, in its vulnerabilities array, every vulnerability that the tree's .github/vex.toml judges not to affect the release, with the reason. A tree with no such judgement has no vex.toml, and its SBOM has no vulnerabilities key. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_01_justification: The standard sets the threshold: actions/dependency-review-action fails a pull request that adds or changes a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/dependency-review.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_05_02_justification: release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares, and every publish job needs it to succeed. An advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id that the tree's own .github/vex.toml, carried into the release's signed SBOM, states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_03_justification: The required lint check audits the whole uv.lock, every dependency group, on every pull request: check_audit.py --all-groups runs uv audit, which reads OSV's malicious-package (MAL-) entries as well as advisories. Any such entry fails the check, and so does an OSV that cannot be reached. The audit's only exemption is a .github/vex.toml entry, reviewed like any other change. The required Dependency review check also blocks a change that adds a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or a licence outside the allow-list. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_06_01_justification: The standard's section 5 sets a threshold of zero for ruff: select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same, in the required lint check. CodeQL runs on every pull request, but the standard sets no threshold for its alerts. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff
osps_vm_06_02_justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: A merged pull request that changes code under src/ also changes tests/, unless it leaves behaviour as it was: a docstring, a comment, a move, a removal or a refactor. The 100% line and branch coverage gate also fails a fix whose new code no test runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
release_notes_justification: RELEASE_NOTES.md holds each release's notes, and release.yml publishes the tag's section as the GitHub release body. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/releases/latest
release_notes_vulns_justification: The release notes name each advisory the release fixes: v2026.10.8 names GHSA-qjpp-8mp6-7744. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/releases/tag/v2026.10.8
repo_distributed_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.
repo_interim_justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39
repo_public_justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.
repo_track_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported on the GitHub issue tracker, through the issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, as CONTRIBUTING.md's *The issue tracker* describes: <https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/issues>. Vulnerabilities go through SECURITY.md instead: <https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md>.
report_responses_justification: Issues #15 to #24, filed by pmazzocchi on 2026-09-30, were all answered and closed by 2026-10-02. Issue #142, filed by pmazzocchi on 2026-10-19, was closed the same day. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed
report_tracker_justification: Each repository uses its own GitHub Issues tracker for individual issues, with issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and an organization-wide tracker in btclib-org/.github for cross-repository findings. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/issues
require_2FA_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member. https://github.com/btclib-org
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md's Roles names the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
secure_2FA_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication and allows only secure methods: TOTP apps, security keys or passkeys, and GitHub Mobile, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
security_review_justification: pmazzocchi, an owner other than the maintainer, reviewed the project on 2026-09-30: https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/issues/26 . The review pins its scope to a commit, checks each claim of ASSURANCE_CASE.md, states what it did not cover and files each finding as an issue.
signed_releases_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing, and each GitHub release a Sigstore provenance bundle. SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/releases/latest
sites_password_security_justification: Project sites are GitHub, PyPI and Read the Docs; this repository runs no site of its own that stores user passwords -- authentication is GitHub's and PyPI's, not this project's. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md
small_tasks_justification: Small tasks for new contributors carry the label "good first issue", which CONTRIBUTING.md sets aside for a first contribution. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's python analysis (codeql.yml) runs on a schedule, on every pull request and on every push to main, and ruff's `select = ["ALL"]` includes the bandit-derived S rules, both FLOSS static-analysis tools looking for common vulnerabilities. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No static-analysis finding is open: CodeQL has no open alert, and ruff and mypy findings fail the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: on every push and pull request: https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/actions/workflows/lint.yml, https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/actions/workflows/codeql.yml
test_branch_coverage80_justification: pyproject.toml sets branch = true under [tool.coverage.run], and the 100% fail_under gate includes branches: https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: test.yml runs the suite on every pull request that changes more than the prose files its prose-pattern names, and on every push to main that changes more than top-level Markdown files. Its aggregate job, test: every job passed, is a required check on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
test_justification: test.yml runs the suite, gated at 100% line and branch coverage, against vectors their authors publish: BIP39's reference implementation's and the Japanese ones BIP39 cites, SLIP-0039's and Electrum's. tests/_data/README.md pins each vendored file to its upstream commit. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md makes 100% coverage a gate every change must pass, so new functionality comes with its tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% line and branch coverage, and fail_under = 100.0 fails the CI gate on any new code without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0, gated on every pull request by test.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_statement_coverage90_justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0 under [tool.coverage.report], and the required test check enforces it on every pull request: https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
tests_are_added_justification: The required check test: every job passed fails any pull request that leaves a line or branch untested. The merged pull requests show recent changes landing with their tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100% coverage gate, so new functionality is not accepted without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: Over the last two releases, v2026.10.24 and v2026.11.2, 34 of 59 pull requests were approved by somebody other than the author, 58%, above the 50% the criterion asks (v2026.11.2 12 of 26, v2026.10.24 22 of 33); 27 were approved by somebody other than fametrano. Counted by merge time between release publications, over the same two-release window on every btclib-org project. main's ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author, and fametrano holds a pull_request-mode bypass of it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
updateable_reused_components_justificati: At runtime the package reuses only the standard library. The test and tooling components are PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock and bumped by Dependabot, and the deps-latest sentinel runs the full suite against the upgraded set every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/.github/workflows/deps-latest.yml
version_semver_justification: CalVer, YYYY.M.D, declared in pyproject.toml and explained in RELEASE_NOTES.md: the number says when a release was cut and promises nothing about compatibility, so a breaking change is announced in RELEASE_NOTES.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
version_tags_justification: Each release is tagged v<version> on the release commit, as RELEASING.md requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/tags
version_tags_signed_justification: Every release tag is signed, and RELEASING.md reads each signature back. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/tags
version_unique_justification: Each release carries a unique calendar version, YYYY.M.D, declared once in pyproject.toml and tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/releases
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No publicly known vulnerability is left unfixed: each published advisory names the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/security/advisories
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Every published advisory names the release that fixes it, and no Dependabot alert is open. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: An advisory credits its reporter as finder. GHSA-qjpp-8mp6-7744 lists pmazzocchi as finder. SECURITY.md's Security review credits the 2026-09-30 review to pmazzocchi. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-review https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: pmazzocchi's security review, filed on 2026-09-30, was answered on 2026-10-01 and closed on 2026-10-03. GHSA-qjpp-8mp6-7744 was published with its fix, v2026.10.8, the day it was opened. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/issues/26 https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/security/advisories
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md's Reporting a vulnerability gives the private channels (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who can see a report, and how a CVE is requested. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are not tolerated: ruff, strict mypy and pytest's filterwarnings = ["error"] fail the required checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_justification: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_strict_justification: ruff runs with `select = ["ALL"]` (every rule family) and mypy runs with `strict = true`; both are zero-finding pre-commit hooks enforced again by the required lint workflow. https://github.com/btclib-org/bip39-slip39/blob/main/pyproject.toml
